column3: With respect to the Hampton Towne Centre Mortgage Loan (2.9%), the borrower sponsor disclosed a prior foreclosure related to a 2011 loan secured by a single-tenant property after the tenant unexpectedly stopped paying rent and vacated. The originating lender sold the loan to a third party, which foreclosed despite the borrower sponsor’s out-of-pocket repositioning and securing a replacement tenant. The borrower sponsor reported that the loan balance was approximately $1,600,000, the note buyer acquired the asset for $900,000, then later sold it for more than $2,400,000, and pursued a $672,000 deficiency, which the borrower sponsor paid.
